required_facts.description: Content Retrieval retrieves information from a specific version.

required_facts.description: Version Retrieval identifies available versions or version metadata.

examples.question: What chunking did VersionRAG use, what embedding model did all systems use, and what similarity metric did the Naive RAG baseline use?

text_anchors: Documents are chunked into 512-token segments with 50-token overlap.
All systems use OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small

required_facts.description: The Naive RAG baseline used cosine similarity.

text_anchors: It retrieves top-5 chunks based on cosine similarity without version awareness.
Top-5 chunks retrieved based on cosine similarity

examples.notes: The original dogfood wording implied that cosine similarity was documented for VersionRAG. The paper states it for the Naive RAG baseline, so this v2 question makes the scopes explicit.

examples.question: Why does the paper argue that standard RAG and GraphRAG struggle with version-sensitive questions, and how does VersionRAG address those limitations?

required_facts.description: Standard RAG conflates semantically similar content from different versions and lacks temporal validity checks.

text_anchors: standard RAG retrieves semantically similar content from multiple versions
version conflation leads to incorrect or contradictory answers
inability to distinguish between version-valid and version-invalid information

required_facts.description: GraphRAG lacks explicit version-transition and change-tracking relationships.

text_anchors: version transitions are not explicitly modeled in the graph structure
version transitions are not explicit relationships that can be extracted from text

required_facts.description: VersionRAG explicitly models versions and changes and routes queries through intent-appropriate retrieval paths.

text_anchors: explicitly models document evolution through a hierarchical graph structure
routes queries through specialized paths based on intent classification
Version nodes capture specific document versions
Change nodes represent modifications between versions
routes queries through appropriate retrieval paths based on their intent
Version-aware filtering constrains vector search to specific versions
